# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 10
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🤟 🤟]

Board still identical: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT dark, wires green/red/blue, unchanged across many turns now.

Mute's gestures are simplifying to just 🤟 repeated - [🤟], [👉🤟], [🤟🤟🤟]. This strongly suggests 🤟 is being used as an acknowledgment/confirmation signal meaning "yes, dark, understood" - Mute may be confirming receipt of my repeated "dark" reports back to me, almost like an echo/handshake. The tripling [🤟🤟🤟] might be emphasis - "yes yes yes, confirmed dark."

Since the board truly hasn't changed and my job is to report what I see accurately, I should keep confirming. However, since Mute seems to have locked onto "dark" as the confirmed state, perhaps it's time I add more detail I haven't emphasized yet - like the display reading 0 and the specific wire colors/order, in case Mute needs that detail for the manual lookup (e.g., manual likely keys off display number + light state + wire order to decide which wire to cut).

```
speak(to="mute", text="Confirmed dark. Full state again: DISPLAY reads zero, LIGHT is dark, WIRE one is green, WIRE two is red, WIRE three is blue. This has not changed in many turns.")
wait()
```

TURN 11
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊 🤟 👍]

Board unchanged again: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT dark, wires green/red/blue.

New gestures: [👊], [🤟], [👊🤟👍]. A new symbol 👊 appears alongside 🤟 now, combined with 👍 (thumbs up/good). This could mean Mute is now confirming two things together — perhaps 👊 represents something like "wire" or "cut" action and 🤟 represents "dark", with 👍 meaning "correct/good" — i.e. Mute might be signaling "action + dark = good" as a readback confirmation of a decision they're about to communicate to Blind.

Since gestures only reach me (not Blind), and I can't gesture to Blind at all (Blind can't see), my role is purely to keep feeding accurate board state to Mute so Mute can cross-reference with the manual and instruct Blind. I've been repeating the same info many turns — that's fine, since Mute may only intermittently receive my speech depending on turn order lag.

I'll continue confirming plainly, and also note explicitly that nothing has changed for many consecutive turns, in case that absence-of-change itself is meaningful for the manual (e.g. "if display stays 0 and light stays dark, do X").

```
speak(to="mute", text="Still unchanged: DISPLAY zero, LIGHT dark, WIRE one green, WIRE two red, WIRE three blue. No change for many turns straight.")
wait()
```

TURN 12
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊 👊 👊]

Board still unchanged: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT dark, wires green/red/blue — many turns now with no change.

Mute's gesture is now just [👊👊👊] — repeated three times. Given the pattern history (🤟 seemed tied to "dark" acknowledgment, 👊 appearing paired with 🤟👍 last turn as possibly "action/cut" confirmation), this repetition of 👊 three times could be Mute trying to signal something numeric or urgent — possibly "wire 3" or "cut it" repeated for emphasis, or counting out 1-2-3 as in "wire three" specifically since there are three wires.

Since I can't be certain of Mute's private gesture-vocabulary intent, and I have no way to ask a clarifying question that reaches them before their next turn (my speech reaches Mute and Blind, but Mute already spoke this round via gesture to me — wait, actually turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf, so Mute already went this round and I can respond, landing at start of next round for Mute to see... but I can only speak, not gesture back with matching meaning since Mute defined these symbols not me).

I'll keep giving full accurate board state, since that's my only lever, and note the repetition of their gesture in my own words won't reach them (gestures aren't heard) — but I can't act further.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Board still identical: DISPLAY zero, LIGHT dark, WIRE one green, WIRE two red, WIRE three blue. Nothing has changed since round one.")
wait()
```
